school: University of Texas at Austin School of Law
gpu: Vista is built on NVIDIA Grace Hopper (GH200) and Grace Superchips — an Arm-based departure from the x86 architecture of Frontera, Stampede and Lonestar6 — connected with NVIDIA NDR InfiniBand at up to 400 Gbps. Frontera and Lonestar6 carry additional GPU subsystems with separately allocated GPU node-hours.
hpcName: Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC) — Vista, Frontera, Lonestar6, Ranch
specs: TACC is a research centre of UT Austin itself, so this is an in-house resource rather than a consortium. Ranch tape archive fronted by roughly 30PB of disk cache. Vista is positioned as the bridge between Frontera (the current NSF leadership-class system) and Horizon, the planned primary system of the NSF Leadership-Class Computing Facility.
notes: ADDED Sept 2026. Texas had exactly one entry in this directory (South Texas College of Law Houston, a standalone school listed separately) despite having around ten ABA-accredited law schools — UT Austin, the state's flagship, was missing. TACC is a research centre of UT Austin, so a UT Austin law faculty member is an in-house user rather than a guest. Two distinct allocation routes exist: TxRAS handles requests from UT Austin, UT System and TACC Partner Institutions, while Vista allocations for UT and UT System researchers go through UT-Austin's Center for Generative AI on a monthly rolling basis. Frontera is separately and broadly available to any US researcher doing open research, with the expectation that work results in publication in a broadly available journal or conference — a condition legal scholarship can generally meet.
caveat: Allocation is competitive and framed around science and engineering. Frontera's policy describes a project PI as 'typically a faculty member or research scientist at a US-based academic institution' and its tracks (LRAC, Pathways, LSCP) are written around code readiness and scaling, with Pathways requiring demonstrated existing research funding for code and algorithm development. Startup and Director Discretionary allocations are the realistic entry points. No evidence was found of a law-school allocation.

hpcName: Roar Collab (Institute for Computational and Data Sciences)
specs: Basic, Standard and High Memory core types; Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8; software stack of roughly 240 applications updated on a schedule. Housed in a University Park data centre with 2.4MW redundant power and 12,000 sq ft of environmentally controlled space, about half of which is dedicated to ICDS infrastructure. GPU pricing includes the Standard cores needed alongside the GPU — 28 for P100, 24 for a full A100, 12 for a half A100.
notes: ADDED Sept 2026. Pennsylvania was missing entirely from this directory despite having roughly nine ABA-accredited law schools. Penn State's Institute for Computational and Data Sciences runs Roar Collab, and ICDS states that it supports faculty from dozens of departments in nearly all of Penn State's twenty-four campuses — which is what brings both of Penn State's law schools into scope. The access model is notably open: every user receives an automatic monthly allocation of READ (Research Exploration And Discovery) credits usable on all hardware types including GPUs, with no action required, and faculty needing more can request additional credits through an online form that ICDS describes as not difficult, with requests under 50 credits processed quickly and minimal information required. One credit is one Basic core-month and costs about $3 if purchased. Note that 'Roar' and 'Roar Collab' are different systems: Roar is a restricted-data environment available only through a paid allocation, while Roar Collab is the general cluster most users should use.
caveat: GPU generation is A100/P100, and the credit economics matter. Roar Collab documents single-GPU and Multi-Instance GPU compute on A100 and P100 only — no H100 was found — so this is 'modern', not frontier. GPU work consumes credits faster than Basic cores, and the automatic monthly READ allocation was being reduced during a transition period, with ongoing amounts from April 2026 announced separately. Check current credit levels before assuming free GPU time.
